To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary management of diabetes is not easy and requires constant effort.

the most common reasons for non-adherence were: non-afford ability of prescribed diet, feeling that temptation was inevitable, difficulty in revealing to the host that one was diabetic, poor attitude of health care providers, irregular diabetes education, limited number of nutrition sessions, and limited spousal and social support.

1) the most common reason for the non adherence of the patients was that they were not aware of their diet and 2) the most important factors that affect the adherence to diet were: the patients' age, their education level and their occupation, their knowledge about their disease and their attitude toward the disease and the diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the factors that contribute to non adherence of the dietary regimen among adult diabetic patients.
the study of factors affecting dietary regimen adherence among diabetic patients.
the factors that influence dietary management non-adherence in diabetic patients and how these factors could be managed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factors that contribute to non-adherence in dietary regimen in adult diabetics are socio-demographic, psychosocial and health care providers related factors.
, there is significant association between socio-demographic, psychosocial and health care providers factors and nonadherent dietary regimen in adult diabetics.
the factors identified were: socio- demographic factors, psychosocial factors and health care providers factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the identified obstacles are the major contributors to the non-adherence to the diet in the study population and that the obstacles identified are modifiable.
there is a need to improve the health system in the country to provide the necessary support to patients with diabetes.
the study has identified several factors that contribute to non-adherence to dietary management among diabetic patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to improve the dietary management of diabetes in Nigeria.
we have a lot of work to do to improve the quality of care and to make it more patient centered.
we need to be more aware of the factors that contribute to nonadherence in patients with diabetes and to develop strategies to help patients overcome them.
